turns.assessment: The failure is a unidirectional, all-channel loss on OMS S18→S03. Crucially, input power is lost at the booster itself and then at every downstream amplifier, while pump currents remain unchanged and the reverse OMS S03→S18 is normal. This localizes the fault ahead of the S18→S03 booster, most consistently to a disconnected/broken OMS input patch at S18 rather than an amplifier or fibre-span failure.

proposals.rationale: The S18→S03 booster input, booster output, every downstream amplifier, receiving channels, and OCM channels all lose signal together. An open input patch at S18 explains this exact cascade. Unchanged amplifier pump currents and a normal reverse direction strongly exclude amplifier failure and a bidirectional cable cut.
A failed S18 ROADM WSS port could block channels before the S18→S03 booster, but the broad all-channel outage at the OMS input is more directly explained by the common output patch being open.
A booster failure would remove downstream output, but it would not explain loss of the booster's own input power; unchanged pump current also weighs strongly against it.
